# WH-002 Cycle Count SOP

## 1. Purpose

### 1.1 Objective
This procedure sets out how Meridian Supply Co. verifies the accuracy of on-hand inventory through continuous counting rather than a single annual shutdown count.

### 1.2 Scope
It applies to every stocked item in the main warehouse and the overflow annex, including items held in the hazmat cage.

## 2. Count Cadence

### 2.1 ABC classification
Items are classified A, B or C by annual consumption value. The Inventory Control team reviews the classification every January and after any major range change.

### 2.2 ABC cadence
Count frequency follows the classification.

| Class | Typical share of items | Count cadence |
|---|---|---|
| A | Highest value | Monthly |
| B | Mid value | Quarterly |
| C | Lowest value | Twice a year (semi-annually) |

A items are therefore counted twelve times a year, B items four times and C items twice. The count schedule is generated by the warehouse system on the first working day of each month.

### 2.3 Event-driven counts
In addition to the schedule, a count is triggered by a negative on-hand balance, a pick short, a receipt adjustment or a customer complaint of a wrong item.

## 3. Performing the Count

### 3.1 Preparation
Pending receipts and putaways for the location are completed before the count. The location is frozen in the system so that no movement posts during the count.

### 3.2 Blind count
The counter is given the location and item only, not the system quantity. The counter enters the quantity found on the handheld.

### 3.3 Count sheet integrity
Counts are never copied from a previous sheet. Partial cartons are counted in units, not estimated.

## 4. Variance Handling

### 4.1 Variance tolerance
A count is accepted without further action when the variance is within ±2% of the system quantity or $250 in value. A variance outside tolerance triggers a recount.

### 4.2 Recount by a different counter
The recount is performed by a different counter from the first one. The second counter is not told the first result. If the two counts agree, the agreed quantity is used. If they disagree, the Inventory Control Manager supervises a third count.

### 4.3 Posting adjustments
Confirmed variances are posted as inventory adjustments under the approval limits and reason codes in WH-005. No adjustment is posted by the counter.

## 5. Root Cause

### 5.1 Investigation
Variances outside tolerance are reviewed within two working days for the likely cause such as mis-pick, mis-labelled putaway, unreported damage or receiving error.

### 5.2 Trend reporting
Inventory Control reports accuracy by zone monthly to the Director of Operations. Zones that miss target for two months in a row receive a process audit.

## 6. Responsibilities

### 6.1 Counters
Counters follow the blind count method, report access problems and never adjust the system quantity.

### 6.2 Supervisors
Warehouse Supervisors release locations for counting and ensure that recounts are done by a different person.

### 6.3 Inventory Control
Inventory Control owns the schedule, the investigation and the accuracy report.

### 6.4 Safety and access
Counters use approved equipment to reach upper racking and never climb racks. Locations that cannot be reached safely are reported and rescheduled, not skipped silently. Hazmat cage counts are done with a second person present.

### 6.5 Accuracy target
The inventory accuracy target is 99% of locations counted without a variance outside tolerance. Results are shown by zone and by counter so that coaching can be targeted.
